subject: Sizing for peak surge windows + pricing path for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@atlas.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing: weekly peak surges + committed pricing options

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this conversation on. Quick summary of Atlas AI's needs so we can get a concrete sizing & commercial path:

- Core feature: real-time summarization + search re-ranking for streaming clinical notes.
- Typical steady state: ~120 reqs/min (short prompts, ~80 tokens output).
- Peak surge windows: 10–12am PST and 6–8pm PST where traffic spikes to ~700 reqs/min sustained for 20–30 mins, with brief micro-peaks up to ~1,500 reqs/min for a couple minutes.
- Context length: avg 2,400 tokens input + 300 tokens output (we usually pass 2.7k context).
- Concurrency: at surge peaks we expect 150–250 concurrent sessions.

We are evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool with 99th-pct throughput guarantees. Procurement is asking for:
1) a recommended pool sizing (instance types + count) to cover steady + surge with 95% confidence,
2) expected token/sec throughput and latency profile at 95/99 pctl,
3) pricing options: monthly reserved commits for 12 vs 24 months, and discount tiers for multi-year/volume, and
4) any suggested burst/fallback strategies (e.g., cheaper model variants) to control cost.

Can you send an initial sizing spreadsheet and a commercial path? We need a ballpark by Friday so Procurement can start a budget review.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director of Engineering
Atlas AI

Team —

Quick notes from the perf model run (I used Rajiv's sample traces):

- Model: mid-sized open transformer (context 3k) mapped to g5x2-equivalent for perf planning (we'll test on our benches for exact kernel mix).
- Steady state (120 reqs/min): 1-2 GPUs, very low utilization (~12–18%).
- Surge baseline (700 reqs/min sustained): ~6 GPUs to keep p95 generation latency under 350ms and p99 under ~750ms (single-token stream).
- Micro-peaks (1,500 reqs/min for 2–3 min): require burst capacity ~12 GPUs if we want <1s p99 latency; otherwise fallback to cheap model variant reduces GPU need to ~6–7 GPUs with p99 ~1.2s.
- Concurrency sizing: to hit 150–250 concurrent sessions with 2.7k context, we need aggressive KV cache handling; expected memory footprint pushes us to 80–90% mem utilization per GPU at peak if we pick 80GB A100-equivalent devices.

Recommendations (first pass):
1) Prod pool: 8x A100-80GB equivalents + 4x burst nodes (autoscalable to 12) — covers sustained surges and short micro-peaks with controlled latencies.
2) Commit tiers: 50% reserved baseline (pay for 8 GPUs monthly) + burst credits billed on usage.
3) Fallback: route low-priority requests to a 3–4x cheaper quantized model during micro-peaks; set a realtime routing policy so critical user journeys are prioritized.

I’ve attached the workbook with simulation tabs (steady/surge/micro-peak). Ben

Rajiv —

Thanks for the patience; attached is a concise proposal:

Summary (short):
- Recommended pool: 8x A100-80GB equivalent baseline + autoscale up to 12 for brief micro-peaks. This balances steady idle with headroom for 1,500 req/min micro-peaks.
- Expected performance (baseline config): P95 single-token generation ~320–380ms during sustained surge, P99 ~700–1,000ms depending on distribution; micro-peak with burst nodes targeted <1s p99.
- Commit pricing paths:
  • 12-month reserved (Baseline 8 GPUs): list $X/month, suggested negotiated discount 18–22% for ATL-2026-1273 with a 30% up-front payment option.
  • 24-month reserved (Baseline 8 GPUs): list $X/month, suggested discount 28–33% with built-in 10% burst-credit allowance.
- SLA & guarantees: we can offer a throughput-backed SLA for the baseline pool (99.5% availability of baseline capacity). Micro-peak latency guarantees are available as a commercial add-on.

Cost-control levers we recommend:
- Intelligent routing: critical requests pinned to baseline pool; non-critical routed to quantized model.
- Autoscale cooldowns & burst credits: short-lived micro-peaks covered by burst nodes to avoid over-committing.
- Monthly commit vs usage banding: a blended model where baseline is committed and excess usage is billed at a discounted overage rate.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: if Atlas is comfortable with the 8→12 pool approach, Ben can convert the numbers into a term sheet and we’ll add the 12/24-month pricing rows.
2) Technical: Marissa will schedule an onboarding call to validate traces against our test harness and run a short canary in your staging.

I’ve attached: redwood-pricing-term-sheet-v2.pdf and the workload workbook (same one Ben referenced).

Would love feedback by Thu so Ben can put final pricing into the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
